A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOI benchmarking work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, although the revised benchmark prevents direct interpretation of score changes as performance gains or losses.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of VLMs and HOI-specific methods under three settings, including DETR-assisted evaluation, in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, dataset analyses and model-error analyses, including Tables 2–4 and 6–7 and Figures 3, 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially changes benchmark construction. After the retained VLM filtering pipeline, v2 introduces manual refinement of every question, removes easy cases, adds temporally plausible positive answers and constructs harder negatives. v1 used existing annotated positives and filtered negatives, with a sampled quality check.

E1.justification: V-COCO-based data is newly used for fine-tuning experiments, extending actual data coverage beyond HICO-DET. Table 1 and Appendix B also add dataset-composition comparisons involving V-COCO, SWiG-HOI and Bongard-HOI. Model evaluation nevertheless remains focused on HICO-DET-derived HOI tasks and the same three settings.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds InternVL3 to its comparison of conventional and proposed benchmark scores. Figure 3 additionally compares pretrained Qwen2.5-VL-7B with two supervised-fine-tuned variants. The principal VLM families and all five HOI-specific comparison methods are retained.

E3.justification: Evaluation changes from 9,338 questions to a refined, redistributed test set of 1,274 images. v2 adds question-averaged precision and recall, removes single-/multi-person reporting, and replaces InternVL2.5-8B with InternVL2.5-38B. It also introduces supervised fine-tuning experiments, including training on 111,459 HICO-DET-derived questions.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantified attribution-error analysis, qualitative failures involving nearby people and occlusion, and head-versus-tail recall analysis before and after fine-tuning. It also analyzes dataset-distribution differences. The earlier single-/multi-person breakdowns disappear, while the DETR diagnostic is retained and updated in Appendix D.2 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both describe randomized answer-option ordering without quantifying variability across orderings.

E6.justification: The main result tables are extensively replaced under the revised test conditions. For example, Qwen2.5-VL-32B's Setting 3 Macro-F1 is 75.79 in v1 Table 3 and 57.25 in v2 Table 4; this is not a same-setting regression. v2 also adds precision/recall scores, fine-tuning results and attribution-error rates, while removing subgroup result entries.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B's mathematical explanation of why pooled Macro-F1 can exceed both subgroup scores, including Equations 5–6 and its illustrative example, is removed. The four principal metric definitions remain mathematically unchanged, despite reordered presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions newly emphasize a deliberately challenging benchmark and specific attribution/detection failures. The conclusion replaces v1's claim that small VLMs surpass specialized methods in recognition-only evaluation with a claim of approximate parity, while describing large VLMs as superior on most metrics.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations involving training-distribution priors, confusion between nearby people's actions, crowded and occluded detection failures, and head-class bias after fine-tuning. Appendix D.2 also interprets fine-tuning as shifting conservative predictions toward higher recall at a precision cost, substantially extending v1's recognition-versus-detection discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly documents full recognition and detection prompts and model-specific bounding-box processing, including Qwen resizing and InternVL coordinate-system queries. Appendix C.3 explains training-question composition. These are substantial documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish that the newly disclosed preprocessing replaced a different earlier implementation. Dataset licensing and release instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds explicit positioning against Bongard-HOI and quantitative benchmark comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix B, alongside citations concerning dataset priors and long-tailed HOI data. The EZ-HOI citation is removed. The central positioning as a unified alternative to exact-match HOI evaluation remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark description, results and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Results are reorganized around named findings and fine-tuning, substantial implementation and DETR discussion moves into Appendix D, and the appendices are reorganized around dataset comparisons, construction details and additional experiments.

P2.justification: Result tables replace subgroup columns with aggregate metrics and precision/recall columns. Figure 2 is replaced with a compact example, with new examples in appendix Figure 4. v2 adds a benchmark-comparison table, fine-tuning displays and failure galleries, and relocates the DETR table. Figure 1 also changes its comparator set and metric labeling.

improvement.justification: v2 improves diagnostic depth and reproducibility through measured attribution errors, fine-tuning/head-tail analyses, and detailed prompts and coordinate handling. It also tempers v1's small-VLM superiority claim. These gains are limited by lost subgroup results, incomplete specification of redistribution and fine-tuning, and Figure 1's conflicting Instance-F1 axis/caption and Macro-F1 legend. The harder, smaller test set alone does not establish better evaluation validity, but the added evidence about model behavior supports a modest net improvement.
